summary: CI flakes: conformance test harness intermittently failing across SDK repos (streaming + 429 burst scenarios)
environment: CI (GitHub Actions): ubuntu-latest runners; observed intermittently on macos-latest as well
description:
Background
- As part of the SDK parity audit, we added a cross-repo conformance test harness (mock gateway + scenario runner) and gated merges on it.
- Since landing initial CI integration, multiple repos have intermittent failures requiring manual reruns (wasting CI minutes + slowing reviews).

Impact
- PRs blocked on “Required checks” despite no code changes related to the failure.
- Retry/streaming changes are high-churn this sprint; flakes are increasing support load for DevEx and slowing rollout.

What’s flaking (top signatures)
1) TypeScript (Node 20, undici/fetch)
- Scenario: streaming / partial SSE frames
- Symptom: test expects N events then timeout / premature EOF
- Example failure:
  - "Error: Timeout waiting for event 'message' (received 7/8)"
  - "TypeError: terminated" (undici) after server closes connection

2) Go
- Scenario: 429 burst + Retry-After handling
- Symptom: occasional extra attempt observed (off-by-one) OR mock server receives fewer requests than expected
- Example failure:
  - "expected 3 requests, got 2" (server logs show client aborted due to context deadline)

3) Python
- Scenario: transport error classification (connection reset) + retry budget
- Symptom: intermittent ConnectionError classification mismatch; appears tied to timing of server startup and port readiness
- Example failure:
  - "ConnectError: [Errno 111] Connection refused" surfaced before mock gateway is listening

Suspected root causes
- Mock gateway readiness: race between test start and server actually accepting connections (especially under CI load).
- Timing assumptions: streaming tests assume tight timing (flush cadence / frame arrival) that is realistic locally but too aggressive on shared runners.
- Port contention / ephemeral ports: sporadic failures around binding to localhost and immediate connect attempts.
- Node/Go runtime differences in CI: scheduler delays leading to missed timeouts and cancellation propagation.

Notes / constraints
- We should not “fix” flakes by adding hidden retries to the SDK clients inside tests; the conformance harness is explicitly validating retry behavior.
- Prefer harness-level stabilization (readiness barrier, deterministic scheduling) over loosening assertions that reduce signal.

Immediate workaround
- Manual rerun of the failing job typically passes on 1–2 reruns.
- Not acceptable as a long-term workflow for required checks.

Proposed stabilization actions
A) Add explicit mock gateway readiness barrier
- Server starts, binds, then exposes /healthz. Test runner waits (with capped timeout) before running scenarios.

B) Remove overly tight streaming timing assumptions
- Assert on event sequence/content, not on inter-event timing.
- Increase streaming scenario per-test timeout budget (CI-only) without changing SDK default timeouts.

C) Reduce test concurrency for scenarios that depend on shared ports
- TS: run streaming suite with --runInBand (or split into separate job shard).
- Go: ensure httptest server per-test, avoid global ports.

D) Add flaky-tracker signal in CI logs
- Print scenario name, seed, runner CPU info, and mock gateway timestamps (bind time, first request time) to correlate.

Acceptance criteria
- Conformance checks pass at >= 99% over 50 consecutive CI runs per repo (python/ts/go) without manual reruns.
- No change to client retry semantics solely to satisfy conformance harness.
- Streaming tests remain meaningful (still detect regressions in SSE parsing/cancellation).

Owner / follow-ups
- Leila (harness): readiness barrier, logging, CI concurrency adjustments.
- Dana / Mateusz / SDK owners: review any assertion changes to ensure we don’t mask real regressions.
resolution: Implemented readiness barrier for mock gateway, relaxed streaming test timing assertions (sequence-based), and reduced concurrency for streaming suite in CI. Added additional debug logging (timestamps + scenario IDs) to make any future flakes actionable. After changes, observed 50/50 green runs on required checks across python/ts/go with no reruns.
comments: 2025-02-06 10:14 PT - Sahana Iyer: Creating internal ticket to track increasing flakes on conformance checks. Seeing ~1/6 PRs need rerun in TS repo, and occasional in Go. Attaching representative logs in the PR threads; consolidating here so we can make a targeted harness fix.

2025-02-06 13:02 PT - Leila Farouk: Took this. First suspicion is mock gateway startup race. In TS logs, first request happens ~5–20ms after "server.listen()" line, but before we see "listening on" print. Will add explicit /healthz and runner wait.

2025-02-07 09:41 PT - Dana Lo: Confirmed TS failures correlate with streaming partial-frame test. Locally I can reproduce by adding CPU load. The test currently expects the 8th SSE event within 1s; CI sometimes takes longer. Agree with switching to sequence/content assertion and bumping scenario timeout budget.

2025-02-07 15:26 PT - Mateusz Zielinski: Go failure shows context deadline exceeded inside test harness, not SDK. The harness sets 2s overall timeout for scenario; under CI it sometimes hits 2s before retries complete (especially when Retry-After=1s). Suggest increasing harness scenario timeout or making it derive from backoff schedule + safety margin.

2025-02-10 11:18 PT - Leila Farouk: PRs up across harness adapters: (1) add /healthz and wait-for-ready with 10s cap, (2) per-scenario timeout defaults increased (non-streaming 5s, streaming 15s) in harness only, (3) TS streaming suite runs in-band on CI. Also added debug timestamps: bind_time_ms, first_request_ms, and scenario_id.
2025-02-11 08:55 PT - Sahana Iyer: Ran 20 consecutive re-runs on a no-op branch in TS: 20/20 green after changes. Prior baseline was 3 failures in 20. Looks promising.

2025-02-12 14:37 PT - Leila Farouk: Go adapter updated to ensure each scenario uses its own httptest server; removed shared global port. Also added explicit cleanup + waitgroup to avoid server closing before client reads final bytes (was causing premature EOF in rare cases).

2025-02-14 10:22 PT - Ibrahim Khan: Please ensure we document this in the conformance test plan so future contributors don’t reintroduce timing-based assertions. The point is semantics, not wall-clock performance.

2025-02-17 16:05 PT - Leila Farouk: Final verification: 50/50 green runs across python/ts/go required checks (no reruns). Marking resolved. If we see recurrence, we now have scenario_id + timestamps to debug without guesswork.
